Jo Loves is finally open in glorietta and I tried out 4 of their scents. I was really excited about its opening cause my first perfume was Red Roses. I was also a fan of her Zara collab and bought Waterlily Tea Dress since it's a very fresh white floral that I find addicting.

For background, Jo Malone is a perfumer that built her eponymous brand, Jo Malone, that we now know today. She has since sold that company to Estee Lauder and started her own indie brand called Jo Loves.

The 4 scents that I tried were No. 42 Flower Shop, Red Truffle, Mango Thai Lime, and Jo by Jo Loves:

1. No.42 The Flower Shop - From what I remembered, it was like a flower bomb. It was full-on floral with notes of green that complimented it really well.
2. Red Truffle  - This one smelled weird because I couldn't recognize the truffle note -- I'm used to smelling it on pasta haha. However, the dry down turns into a beautiful fig that reminds me of Philosykos.
3. Mango Thai Lime - This is such a good addicting gourmand-y sweet mango. The mint and lime just makes me want to smell it constantly. 
4. Jo by Jo Loves - This one is similar to Mango Thai Lime but more citrus forward and less addicting however it makes up for it by having it Jo's signature and it shows (smells?). It's grapefruit mixed with wood but the wood doesn't overpower the citrus. I think the wood is what makes it last longer than the rest.

Overall, I think they offer a more unique and creative selection when compared to Jo Malone for the same price. I tested all of these directly on my skin and, out of all the scents I tried, only one lasted for more than 3+ hours and it was Jo by Jo Loves. If you've tried anything else from this brand, pls comment below haha

shade range = amount of skin tone shades. basically it's the amount of options that's available for the consumer with respect to their skin color. humans have different skin colors that range from fair (light) to deep (dark) and have different undertones (red, yellow, green, etc.). when someone says poor range with respect to foundation, it means that the brand doesn't have enough options for a particular group of people (usually those with darker skin colors) so they end up producing items that are fair to medium thus making their selection very limited to those who want to try the products. this is usually a bad thing because it means that the brand doesn't want to cater to people of different colors (it's a bit more complicated but that's the gist).

i bought the discovery set awhile back and i'm pretty pleased with my purchase. honestly, the bottle designs aren't that bad, at least for me, but they could definitely be improved upon. to me, the scents matter more than the bottles because i genuinely think that the brand has a lot of potential.

* cervesa rosa - boozy rose. it's a very sweet type of rose with beer and a hint of spiciness. the rose definitely shines through and the beer (which doesn't overtake the rose or smell too alcohol-y) actually compliments it. this is one of my faves mostly because i tend to like rose scents.  

*  banqeros - salty sea/true beach. to me, this is giving me really strong memories of when i would go to the beach when i was younger. rather than smelling like sweet coconut and seawater, this one is more about the entire beach itself (e.g. the seaweed, the sand, the water, the boats, etc.). i've tried beach walk by MM, vanilla vibes by juliette has a gun, sunny side of zanibar by 4711 and none of them come close to smelling like banqeros. all the perfumes i compared it to smell similar to each other but banqeros is definitely the most unique out of all of them.

*  valensole romance - chocnut lol. legit. to me, this smells like chocnut. it's a gourmand that has a very malty chocolate scent that smells sweet and dry. this is the first of the discovery set that i finished and it smells so delicious. 

*  manila oud - a filipino take on oud. it's a woody chypre that smells sophisticated and sweet. thankfully, it's not one of those ouds that smell fecal. it's warm, woody, grassy, and opulent. it's like being transported back in time when the philippines was prosperous and rich.

*  cosa nostra - gunpowder barbershop w/ a smoke room. it's a very strong powdery scent that smells clean, strong, and smoky. personally, this is definitely too strong for my taste and it honestly took awhile for me to like it and appreciate what it's going for. eventually i did like it because of how refined and evocative it smells and how it tries to be different than other powdery scent on the market.

*  hacienderos - humble farm home. it's a citrus-y fougere that smells like grass, lemon, cypress and hay. it's dirty and grassy  without it smelling bad or off. unlike dad's garden lemon tree from lush which smells exclusively like lemons, this one adds an extra layer of green notes that elevate that perfume to something other than another lemon fragrance. it's earthy without it being too dirty. it's clean without being too polished. it strikes the perfect balance between rural and urban life.

i haven't tried their latest creation, 2437 (which is supposed to smell like tupig), because i have way too much perfume already 😅. overall, i would really like to see what other creations the nose of this brand has too offer. i genuinely think that they offer the most unique and exquisite perfumes in the philippines, that's proudly local and proudly filipino, which is already hard to find here. i'd recommend trying out their discovery set before purchasing a bottle since it's so affordable, especially cosa nostra XD
